$comment: The registry of entry points that take UNTRUSTED input (a parser, a sync-frame decoder, an HTTP or MCP JSON-RPC body, a loro import, JSON across the wasm boundary, a font file), and the one list the fuzz targets are derived from (QR-28b, QR-29a). Read by `cargo xtask inputs`. Keys are `<crate>::<path to the entry function>`; `crate` repeats the key's crate and must be in crates/architecture-map.json. Each entry declares maxBytes it will read, maxDepth it will recurse or nest, maxMillis it may run, optionally maxNodes it will build, and the `fuzzTarget` in crates/fuzz that exercises it. A missing cap, a target with no entry and an entry with no target all fail. `pnpm rust:fuzz:*` runs a target with libFuzzer's -max_len at maxBytes and -timeout at maxMillis rounded up to a second. `template: true` marks the one entry that is not an untrusted-input entry: it carries the fuzz pipeline until the first ported parser lands, and its caps bound the fuzzer rather than a refusal in the function.

whiteboard-det::utf16::len.reason: template entry: a flat string, so depth 1; 4 KiB keeps libFuzzer's executions per second high, and 100 ms is far above the microseconds a 4 KiB length takes

whiteboard-wasm::spatial_edges::edge_rou.reason: the routing wire is a flat f64 array the shim builds but any holder of the wasm glue can call. maxBytes is MAX_WIRE_NUMBERS (32768) x 8, the export's own refusal: the largest corpus board's wire is 22984 bytes (clustered 12x12, 144 nodes and 165 edges), so the cap is 11.4x that; a board past it is answered by the TypeScript. maxDepth 2 is the deepest counted group (an edge's bend list inside the edge list); the decoder is iterative. maxMillis 5000 is 2.2x the slowest draw measured at the cap: 2.3 s on Node wasm for a 920-node, 2065-edge board of 251624 bytes, straight edges

whiteboard-wasm::okf::okf_parse.reason: the export reads a document's head, the fences and the frontmatter between them, so any holder of the wasm glue can call it. maxBytes is the frontmatter's own cap (frontmatter::MAX_BYTES, which whiteboard-codec::okf::parse inherits), 768 KiB: a markdown document holds at most MARKDOWN_MAX_CHARS (256 Ki) UTF-16 units and a unit is at most three UTF-8 bytes, so the head of any document the model admits is within it and the TypeScript is never asked instead (owner decision q37). The export refuses a head past it before reading it. The body is not in the head: the shim cuts the head at the closing fence and keeps the body, so a body of any size is read and its size is no input to this cap (a UTF-16 length is never over its UTF-8 one, so the shim's own check on the head refuses nothing the export would take). A lone surrogate in the head crosses as a mark the host chooses, which the export looks for among the strings and keys it read. maxDepth 64 is the YAML reader's MAX_PARSE_DEPTH, the deepest it recurses; the answer is built by one walk of what it produced and adds no nesting beyond one array per mapping or list. maxMillis 2000 is 7.3x the slowest draw measured on Node wasm at the cap, 272 ms for 786414 bytes of 87k integer keys that JavaScript enumerates first (165 ms for preserved keys, 122 ms for a flow list of ~131k integers, 97 ms for a type that is a mapping with a long length list, 91 ms for trust events with extra keys, 57 ms for tags); the codec's own 1000 ms is native, this one carries the wire on wasm

whiteboard-wasm::okf::okf_serialize.reason: the export reads the wire of a frontmatter (JSON in the value wire of okf_wire.rs), so any holder of the wasm glue can call it with bytes of its choosing, which is the decode the fuzz target drives. maxBytes 4718592 is six times the parse entry's 768 KiB, so that any frontmatter the reader would take is written by the core rather than the TypeScript (owner decision q37): the wire is larger than the YAML it spells, and the densest case is a number, 24 bytes of wire (a double's 64 bits in hex) against at least 6 of YAML (`  - 0` and its line break, a list at the root mapping's first level), about 4x; a string or a key costs no more in the wire than in YAML, a control character 6 bytes of JSON escape against 4 of YAML. `okf.rs` holds a frontmatter of zeros at the reader's cap within it. A wire past it is refused before it is parsed. maxDepth 64 is the writer's nesting cap (MAX_PARSE_DEPTH): a deeper value answers unwritable, and serde_json's own 128-level recursion limit (deny.toml bans unbounded_depth) sits above it because the wire spends one array level per mapping or list. maxMillis 3000 is 6.9x the slowest draw measured on Node wasm at the cap: 436 ms for 4718533 bytes of trust events with extra keys (422 ms for tags, 369 ms for integer-like keys under facetsRaw, which the canonical order sorts and JavaScript's enumeration puts first, 300 ms for facet keys, 213 ms for a string of escapes, 196 ms for a list of numbers, 179 ms for one long string). A search of the held keys for each preserved key had made a 16k-key record 147 ms, and quadratic; the writer indexes them now. A refusal names every place a value has no spelling and each place repeats its whole path, so the walk stops once the faults weigh MAX_FAULT_BYTES (1 MiB: the keys of each path, 8 bytes a step and 32 a fault) and the export answers input-too-large. Unbounded, 60 nested 1000-byte keys over 5000 NaN leaves in a 185 KB wire answered 301 MB in 4.6 s and 1.3 GB of resident memory on Node wasm; bounded, the same wire is refused in 15-19 ms at 63 MB. Within the budget the slowest answer measured is 18 ms for 3000 NaN leaves under 20 keys (a 548 KB answer), and 12 ms for 2000 (365 KB); 6000 NaN keys and 8000 keys holding a byte-order mark took 9 ms each

whiteboard-codec::frontmatter::parse.reason: the OKF frontmatter YAML reader takes the text between a document's fences, from a file, an import or a sync, so any holder of a document can call it. maxBytes is MAX_BYTES, the function's own refusal (a longer text answers TooLarge before it is read), 768 KiB: a markdown document holds at most MARKDOWN_MAX_CHARS (256 Ki) UTF-16 units and a unit is at most three UTF-8 bytes, so the frontmatter of any document the model admits is within it (owner decision q37). maxDepth 64 is MAX_PARSE_DEPTH: past MAX_DEPTH (32) the visit refuses, and the parse recurses to 64 only so that a document malformed further down is named malformed first; deeper is refused outright. maxMillis 1000 is 7.9x the slowest draw measured natively in release at the cap: 127 ms for 786414 bytes of 87k integer keys (91 ms for preserved keys, 77 ms for keys under facets, 36 ms for trust events, 28 ms for tags, 23 ms for a flow sequence of ~131k integers and for a type that is a mapping with a long list)

whiteboard-canvas-render::sfnt::Sfnt::pa.reason: the font measurer's reader takes the bytes of a font a user installed into the daemon, so anything that can put a file in the fonts directory reaches it. maxBytes is MAX_BYTES (32 MiB), refused before a byte is read: an ordinary face is a few hundred KiB (the vendored Roboto faces are 349-379 KB) and a CJK face tens of MiB. maxDepth 1: the table directory, `cmap` subtables and `hmtx` are flat arrays read by index and nothing recurses. maxMillis 500 is 29x the slowest draw measured at the cap natively in release, 17 ms for 33552652 bytes holding 2796036 sorted format 12 groups (540 ms in a debug build, which is why it is not tighter; 100000 lookups in that font took 10 ms): the reader allocates nothing and its only loops are the directory scan (at most 65535 records), the cmap record scan (at most 65535) and one validation pass over a subtable's segments or groups (at most a file's length over 12), after which a lookup is a binary search

whiteboard-codec::okf::parse.reason: the OKF envelope reads a whole document from a file, an import or a sync, so any holder of one can call it. maxBytes is the frontmatter's own cap (frontmatter::MAX_BYTES, 768 KiB, the bound on any document the model admits), the refusal parse inherits: the text between the fences is read only up to it, and past it the answer is a YAML refusal. The body is not read at all: the closing-fence search scans it once and it is copied once, so it is not capped (the TypeScript has no cap either) and fuzzing at the frontmatter's cap covers the shapes that cost. maxDepth 64 is MAX_PARSE_DEPTH, the deepest the YAML reader recurses; the schema and the key reordering walk what it produced and add no nesting. maxMillis 1000 is 7.3x the slowest draw measured natively in release at the cap: 138 ms for 87k integer keys that JavaScript enumerates first (99 ms for preserved keys, 92 ms for refused facet keys, 77 ms for a type that is a mapping with a long length list, which the schema renders to a string to measure it, 41 ms for trust events with extra keys, 34 ms for tags, 25 ms for a flow list), and a 16 MiB body took 4.4 ms, 15.7 MiB of near-miss fences 19 ms and 21 MiB of CRLF near-misses 26 ms

whiteboard-codec::json_canvas::parse.reason: the JSON Canvas reader takes a whole board from a file, an import, a paste or a sync, so any holder of one can call it. maxBytes is json_canvas::MAX_BYTES, the function's own refusal (a longer text answers Declined(TooLarge) before it is read, and the caller asks the TypeScript, which has no cap): a board of a few thousand nodes is a few hundred kilobytes, so 4 MiB is far above any board and bounds the fuzzer's cost. maxDepth 64 is json::MAX_DEPTH: the document nests six levels deep before a facet payload begins, and a text nested past 64 answers Declined(TooDeep) the moment the 65th level opens, whatever follows it. maxMillis 2000 is 2.6x the slowest draw measured natively in release: 773 ms for a 4 MiB text of 270k integer-like keys in one facet payload (the reader builds the tree, then puts JavaScript's enumeration order on every object). The other shapes tried at the cap took 10 to 717 ms (a payload of wide arrays nested 55 deep 717, 270k keys at the root 258, 270k facet keys 189, a node list 98 to 111, an edge list refused for its ends 142, a list of invalid nodes 494, a 4 MiB string 11), and a node list written back took 98 to 144 ms in the extended and strict modes

whiteboard-wasm::json_canvas::json_canva.reason: the export reads a whole board's text, so any holder of the wasm glue can call it. maxBytes and maxDepth are whiteboard_codec::json_canvas's own (MAX_BYTES, MAX_DEPTH): the export refuses a text past the first before reading it and the shim then answers from the TypeScript, which has no cap, and a text nested past the second answers a decline the same way. maxMillis 3000 is 2.6x the slowest draw measured on Node wasm, 1146 ms for a 3.82 MiB list of nodes the schema refuses (the others at the cap took 24 to 738 ms: 738 for 270k integer-like keys in one facet payload, 598 for facet keys at the root, 569 for wide arrays nested 55 deep, 544 for 3.84 MiB of valid text nodes, 498 for edges refused for their ends, 24 for one 4 MiB string); the codec's own 2000 is native, this one carries the answer's wire on wasm.

the export reads the wire of a canvas (JSON in the value wire of json_canvas_wire.rs), so any holder of the wasm glue can call it with bytes of its choosing, which is the decode the fuzz target drives. maxBytes is the parse entry's, so a canvas the reader would take is within it as text; the wire of a canvas is about 18% bigger than the text written from it, so a board whose text is over about 3.4 MiB is past the cap and is answered by the TypeScript, and a wire past it is refused before it is parsed. maxDepth 128 is serde_json's own recursion limit (deny.toml bans unbounded_depth), which one array per object or list spends one level of each; the writer's cap is the same, and the shim sends nothing past 100. maxMillis 1000 is 2.9x the slowest draw measured on Node wasm, 344 ms for a canvas holding 250k integer-like facet keys (the extended mode; the others took 80 to 309 ms: 309 for the 11,000-node board in the strict mode, 221 extended, 212 for 120k facet keys at the root, 197 for 150k nested lists, 107 for 300k tags)

whiteboard-wasm::facet_write::facet_buck.reason: the export reads a facets bucket and the workspace's stored stencil library as two texts of the value wire of okf_wire.rs, so any holder of the wasm glue can call it with bytes of its choosing, which is the decode the fuzz target drives. maxBytes 8388608 counts the two together. The largest bucket a write arrives in is the MCP body limit, 4 MiB (packages/mcp-server/src/server/app.ts); the wire spells a number as 24 bytes of hex bits where JSON spells it in one or more, and maxNodes bounds how many there can be, 131072 x 24 = 3 MiB, so 4 + 3 = 7 MiB, rounded up to 8 MiB. A call past it is declined and the TypeScript answers. maxDepth 64 counts the bucket's own mapping as the first level, so a payload nests 63 deep; serde_json's own 128-level recursion limit (deny.toml bans unbounded_depth) sits above it because the wire spends one array per mapping or list. maxNodes 131072 (2^17) is the values the bucket and the library hold together, a mapping, a list or a scalar each one: a facet payload is a handful and a library is at most 256 stencils, so this is two orders above any write a schema takes. It is there because the cost of a refusal is superlinear in the values refused, which bytes do not bound: a tag library of 230k invalid keys, 4.2 MB of JSON, took 4.7 s on Node wasm and answered 17.6 MB, the same shape at 8 MB took 15.7 s, and at the node cap the same payloads take well under half a second; a call past it is declined and the TypeScript answers. maxMillis 3000 is 7.1x the slowest draw measured on Node wasm at the caps, 421 ms for 43k tag values each refused (2.0 MB of wire, a 5.3 MB answer); the others at the caps took 233 ms for a library write of 256 stencils whose facets each refuse (a 3.0 MB answer), 176 ms for 43k invalid tag keys (a 3.2 MB answer), 151 ms for 32k facets of one key each, 150 ms for 131k numbers (3.3 MB), 91 ms for integer-like keys that JavaScript enumerates first, 88 ms for one 8 MiB string, 86 ms for 65k unregistered keys and 61 ms for 26k refused at their version

whiteboard-markdown::parse.reason: the markdown parser reads a document's body from a file, an import, a sync or a paste, so any holder of a document can call it. maxBytes is limits::MAX_BYTES, the function's own refusal (a longer text answers TooLarge before a byte is read), 768 KiB: a markdown body holds at most MARKDOWN_MAX_CHARS (256 Ki) UTF-16 units and a unit is at most three UTF-8 bytes, so every body the model admits is read (owner decision q37). maxDepth is limits::MAX_DEPTH, the deepest nesting of events the tree it builds may have, which bounds the recursion of dropping and walking it to far under a 1 MiB wasm stack (a tree at the cap is built, walked and dropped on a 1 MiB thread stack by tests/limits.rs); block containers are held to 32 by the prescan and the events, the figure the TypeScript tokenizer stops at, and inline nesting is held by the 1,024 delimiter runs one inline run may hold. maxMillis 20000 is 7.1x the slowest draw measured natively in release at the byte cap: 2810 ms for 786000 bytes of `[a](b) ` (112k links in one paragraph; 2007 ms for 98k images, 1756 for 393k lines of `!`, 1686 for 196k one-letter items, 1621 for a table of 131k rows, 706 ms for 30k definitions and 60k references to none, 799 ms for the text `www._` repeated, which runs out its fuel at 75.5 M units and is refused). Fuel (limits::fuel_for) is 96 units a byte and the dearest ordinary shape measured spends 69 (68.5 before the second autolink pass over the finished text was charged), the repository's own markdown files at most 20.5 (16 before it), and a text built to be quadratic (`a* `, `*a_ `, `a~ `, `www._`, images nested in each other's text: 663 ms at the cap) is refused rather than run: unbounded, `a* ` repeated to 256 KB took 10.7 s in the upstream parser on wasm, and `www._` 128 KB took 46 s natively. Fuel was 64 a byte (dearest ordinary 46, repository files 10, slowest draw 2104 ms) until the resolvers' walks over the events and a text's bytes were charged

whiteboard-wasm::spatial_layout::layout_.reason: the export reads a query (the value wire of json_canvas_wire.rs: one mapping whose `query` names the layout piece a root calls on its own, the rest its arguments), so any holder of the wasm glue can call it with bytes of its choosing, which is the decode the fuzz target drives. An `edges` query is a canvas request and is held to every cap the whole layout's entry holds a canvas to (MAX_ELEMENTS on the elements and the expansion ids, the bodies, comment, proposal and fragment caps), since its routing is the whole layout's; a `node-size` or `node-content` query's node body to MAX_BODY_BYTES and its fragment table to MAX_FRAGMENTS; a `label-obstacles` query's nodes to MAX_ELEMENTS and its runs to MAX_RUNS (four per element), because each run is looked up among the frames and the query costs their product, which bytes do not bound. The geometry queries (`label-placement`, `comment-bubble`, `outline-content-box`) cost a fixed number of candidates times the obstacles and the path, which maxBytes bounds. maxBytes 8388608 and maxDepth 128 are the whole layout's, for the same reasons (a call past maxBytes is refused before it is read, and the TypeScript answers; serde_json's own recursion limit), as are the element caps, the own canvas's and the referenced canvases' apart. maxNodes 4096 is MAX_ELEMENTS. maxMillis 60000 is 2.58x the slowest draw measured on Node wasm at the caps, the edge layer of the hub of 2047 edges to 2047 boxes, labelled: 23.2 s, the side search spending its whole budget as the whole layout's does (22.9 s at S15g). At the raised caps (S18f), the edge layer of the hub beside a referenced nested hub took 19.4 s, and with three 768 KiB bodies beside it 21.6 s. The others: 4.5 s for a node holding a 768 KiB table under the ratio floor, which lays the body out twice (3.3 s for 112k links), 0.45 s for a label on a rounded path of 200k points, 0.18 s for 4096 frames and 16384 runs, 0.13 s for a compose bubble against 62k obstacles and 0.09 s for a label against them

the export reads a layout request (the value wire of json_canvas_wire.rs: the canvas, the measurer by name, the options and the reference wire), so any holder of the wasm glue can call it with bytes of its choosing, which is the decode the fuzz target drives. A request naming a `kind` is a markdown body instead (a note, `markdown`, or a comment's prose, `comment`), read as strictly and held to the same caps: its body with every referenced body under the bodies cap, its referenced canvases under the referenced cap, its fragment table under the table's. Past a cap the request is refused, and a host draws the refusal as a notice (owner decision q81, D7). A font-table measurer is named by the handle register_layout_fonts answered, so no face crosses here. maxBytes 8388608 is the request alone, so a request at the bodies cap beside a full canvas fits: a canvas's own wire is a few hundred KB at the element cap and the biggest request measured from real content is 1.8 MB; a call past it is refused before it is read. maxDepth 128 is serde_json's own recursion limit (deny.toml bans unbounded_depth), which the value wire spends one array per mapping or list of; the shim sends nothing past 100. maxNodes 4096 is MAX_ELEMENTS: the nodes, edges and lines of the request's own canvas, above the model's 2,000 nodes and 2,000 edges and lines, refused past it, because what a layout costs is its routing, which bytes do not bound; the expansion policy's id list is held to the same cap, since each id names a file node and every file node is asked against every id. Every canvas the request references is held apart, to as many elements again (MAX_REFERENCED_ELEMENTS, at least the 4,000 the keepers' reference walk loads), since each canvas is routed on its own and the two add; what a layout draws of them is bounded below that by the composer's own nested-element budget, one model-maximal board (4,000), past which a file node draws its card. The bodies are bounded apart (MAX_BODY_BYTES, 3 MiB together, the keepers' reference budget of 4 x 256 Ki UTF-16 units at three bytes each with room for a board's own content, each comment thread's opening message among them, since it is the one a bubble lays out), since a body's cost is its parse and its typesetting and maxBytes alone would let a request repeat the dearest one; one parse stays bounded by the parser's own 768 KiB, so the cap bounds how many parses run. The comment layer is bounded apart too (MAX_COMMENT_ITEMS, the element cap, on the threads, on the obstacles and on the node-set ids across threads; MAX_PASSAGES, a quarter of it, on the passages), because each bubble is placed against every box and every earlier bubble, each node-set id is looked up against every node and each passage is looked for through its node's whole text, so the layer's cost is a product bytes do not bound: 4096 passages over one 768 KiB body took 46.3 s, 1024 take 9.9 s. The proposal layer is bounded apart too (MAX_PROPOSALS, half the element cap, on the proposals; MAX_PROPOSAL_CHANGES, the element cap, on their changes together; MAX_PRIOR_FACET_ENTRIES, the element cap, on the mapping entries the priors' facets hold at every depth together; MAX_BUBBLES, the element cap, on the threads and the proposals together, since each bubble of either layer is placed against every earlier one of both), because each proposal's bubble is placed against every box, every outline and every earlier bubble, and a prior's facets are compared to the element's in any key order, at the square of their entries: 4096 proposals over the hub of 2047 edges took 31.4 s and 2048 took 24.7 s, one prior of 120k entries reversed against the edge's own took 27.8 s (0.1 s at the cap), and both layers at their own caps over the hub took 45.6 s, which MAX_BUBBLES refuses. Refused as proposals. A table of rendered fragments (`fragments`, the math blocks and fences a host typeset ahead) is bounded apart: MAX_FRAGMENTS, the element cap, on its rows, and MAX_PLACED_BYTES, maxBytes, on the markup one layout places, a block past it drawing its fallback, since one row is placed once per block that asks for it and a small body repeating one source would otherwise draw the table many times over; the placements are counted as the layout asks, so a body cut to its box is charged for blocks it does not draw. The rows are searched rather than indexed, since a map's code cost more of the artifact than the search costs a layout at the caps. At those caps on Node wasm: 1.2 s for 87k blocks of one source missing through 4096 rows, 1.1 s for the same blocks answered by the last row searched, 1.0 s for 4096 rows answering 61k sources, 0.9 s for 61k distinct display-math sources in one 768 KiB body with an empty table (every one asked for, a 9.1 MB answer), 0.9 s for 38k mermaid fences asked, 0.8 s for 87k placements of one 40-byte row (11.1 MB), 0.6 s for the same body over a 60-byte row (past the placed cap, measured at the 4 MiB request cap), and 0.1 s for two placements of one 2 MB row. maxMillis 100000 is 1.56x the slowest draw measured on Node wasm at the raised caps, measured at S18f with the shipped build: 60.7, 61.4 and 64.2 s over three runs for the hub of 2047 edges to 2047 boxes with every comment cap at once (4096 threads on the spokes, 1024 of them passages, and 4096 obstacles) and a file node drawing a nested hub of 1999 edges, the most one nested board draws (the hub alone took 16.1-16.4 s, the hub with the nested one 33.8 s, the hub with the nested one and three 768 KiB bodies of the repository's own markdown drawn in file nodes 38.7 s, 3 MiB of those bodies drawn in four file nodes 1.5 s, and 4096 boxes beside a drawn board of 4000 0.5 s). Before the raise, maxMillis 60000 was 1.49x the slowest draw measured on Node wasm at the caps, measured at S15h: 40.2 s for every comment cap at once over the hub of 2047 edges to 2047 boxes (4096 threads on the spokes, 1024 of them passages, and 4096 obstacles; the hub alone took 16.0 s that day), which no proposal cap reaches: 31.8 s for 2048 threads beside 2048 proposals, 34.7 s for 3072 beside 1024, 21.1 s for the hub with 2048 proposals of two changes each (a patch to a spoke and the removal of its edge, compared by value), 7.9 s for 2048 proposals of two patches over 4096 boxes, 4.9 s for 2048 edges each removed by its own proposal, 4.4 s for 2048 proposals about one node, 0.3 s for one proposal adding 4096 boxes. As S15g measured, without the hub, at 2.35x: 25.5 s for every comment cap at once (4095 boxes, 3072 threads on them, 1024 passages through a 560 KB body, 4096 obstacles; 20.0 s for 4096 threads on a grid of boxes with 4096 obstacles, 15.9 s for 4096 threads on one point, 0.1 s for two node sets naming 4096 ids); without comments, 22.9 s for a hub of 2047 edges to 2047 boxes (the side search spends its whole budget; 1023 edges took 14.6 s, 511 took 11.0 s); the others took 6.2 s for a 768 KiB body holding a table of 131k rows, 3.8 s for 1365 boxes and 2730 straight edges (2.6 s orthogonal), 3.1 s for 196k list items, 3.0 s for 2048 boxes and 2048 edges, 2.4 s for 112k links in one paragraph, 1.9 s for 40 file nodes drawing canvases that nest to the depth cap, 0.9 s for 4094 labelled edges between one pair, 0.7 s for 4096 boxes each holding a sentence, and 0.3 s for 4096 bare boxes

whiteboard-wasm::spatial_layout::registe.reason: the export reads the faces a font-table measurer will read (the value wire of json_canvas_wire.rs: a list of family, bold, italic and a range of the bytes) and the bytes they point into, parses every face and keeps a copy, answering the handle a layout request names its measurer by (owner decision q76), so any holder of the wasm glue can call it with bytes of its choosing, which is the decode the fuzz target drives. maxBytes 67108864 counts the bytes and the faces' wire together, and is also the most an instance holds across every live handle, the bytes of the faces it read and their family names together (MAX_HELD_BYTES; a face it cannot read is dropped and holds nothing): two faces at the sfnt reader's own cap (whiteboard-canvas-render::sfnt::MAX_BYTES, 32 MiB, which refuses a larger face as input-too-large face), where the daemon's vendored Roboto is four faces of 1.45 MB; a call past it is refused before it is read, and the layout is answered by the TypeScript. The faces' ranges may not add up to more than the bytes (input-too-large face-bytes), because every layout over the handle reads each face again in time linear in its range: overlapping ranges would charge each layout for the same bytes many times over. maxDepth 128 is serde_json's own recursion limit (deny.toml bans unbounded_depth); an honest wire nests two lists deep. maxNodes 64 is MAX_FACES, the faces one registration holds; MAX_HANDLES (64) bounds the registrations an instance holds at once. maxMillis 2000 is 15x the slowest draw measured on Node wasm at the cap: 132 ms for 67108503 bytes holding two faces of 2796163 sorted format 12 groups each (50-82 ms once warm); a layout over that handle took 34-58 ms against about 1 ms over the vendored faces, the re-read of both faces, which the layout entry's own 60 s holds
